title: Ignatius to the Romans
hook: he begs the Roman Christians not to save him from the beasts
tomorrow: what does a blacksmith's anvil know about courage?

segments.voice: A week of voices. Julian: prayer ones. Catherine: dictated in prayer, walk the bridge, the inner cell, tears of love. And yesterday the Didache's loaf, grain from many hills: gathered into one.
screen: `PRAYER ONES · DICTATED IN PRAYER.` → `WALK THE BRIDGE · THE INNER CELL.` → `TEARS OF LOVE · GATHERED INTO ONE.`

segments.voice: When someone you love is in trouble, the instinct is to fix it: make the call, find the right person, get them out. A man under guard, on his way to Rome, writes ahead to the Christians there and asks them not to. A gentle note for younger listeners: this is the letter of a man facing death for his faith, and it's told simply.
screen: `MAKE THE CALL, GET THEM OUT.` → `A MAN UNDER GUARD WRITES AHEAD.` → `PLEASE DON'T.`

segments.voice: His name is Ignatius, and in this letter he calls himself the bishop of Syria. He's being taken to Rome to face wild beasts. From Syria to Rome, he writes, he is already fighting beasts, and he means the soldiers guarding him, whom he calls leopards, men who only get worse when they're treated kindly. He asks the Roman Christians not to show him a kindness at the wrong time. Then the line the letter is remembered for: I am God's wheat, ground by the teeth of the beasts, so that I may be found pure bread of Christ. Notice the bread again, one day after the Didache's loaf. There, grain from many hills gathered into one. Here, one man, ground like grain, offered as bread. He isn't chasing pain for its own sake; the letter keeps speaking of reaching God. And he doesn't ask for nothing. He asks them to pray for him, and to remember his church in Syria in their prayers. Catholics honor him as a saint and a martyr.
screen: `THE BISHOP OF SYRIA, UNDER GUARD.` · `DON'T SHOW ME KINDNESS AT THE WRONG TIME.` · `GROUND LIKE WHEAT, MADE BREAD.` · `PRAY FOR ME; REMEMBER SYRIA.` · then, large: `GOD'S WHEAT.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person facing real danger this week: someone in a hospital, on a hard road, in a risky job. If a message would fit, send them one plain line that you're thinking of them; if not, simply hold their name until the sit ends. Those who pray can pray for them by name, the way Ignatius asked to be prayed for.
Ignatius to the Romans. A bishop under guard asks his friends for prayer instead of rescue, and calls himself God's wheat.
Your line: God's wheat. Ground like grain, and still meant to become bread. Two weeks, done.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Ignatius of Antioch each year, and his letters are read in the Liturgy of the Hours; the wheat line is among those Catholics quote about martyrdom.

chat.says: tío Javier's crew drives to the coast tonight for storm repairs. downed lines. what do i even text him?
options: Something short: you're praying for him and the crew. Ignatius asked friends for prayer, not speeches.
Beg him to stay home. Real love talks someone out of anything risky, whatever it is.

chat.meaning: Ignatius didn't ask for rescue speeches; he asked to be prayed for and remembered. A short, true message and a prayer fit someone heading into danger.
